name: MIDORI.so Nakameguro
card: An ivy-covered ruin turned into a two-building shared office
title: MIDORI.so Nakameguro — a shared office in two buildings, restored from an ivy-covered ruin
lead: MIDORI.so Nakameguro is in Aobadai, Nakameguro. Its operator, Mirai Institute, was founded on 5 January 2011 and runs eight sites of its own in Tokyo. Nakameguro is “a shared office converted from an abandoned, ivy-covered house”, made up of two buildings: the main house and the old residence. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Two buildings: main house (2F, 3F) and old residence (1F, 2F)
hero_cap: The Nakameguro site, restored from an ivy-covered building
concept: When you're enjoying yourself, ideas come naturally

MIDORI.so is a coworking community exploring “the future of work in a society that values the individual”. Freelancers, small companies and employees of large organisations — of different professions, nationalities and hobbies — work side by side. Its motto: “When you're enjoying yourself, ideas come naturally.”

The Nakameguro site was born from the renovation of an abandoned, ivy-covered house. The third floor of the main house holds the workspace, lounge, meeting room and gallery; the old residence holds private offices. It is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, with a kitchen, lockers and free drinks.
steps: 01 · Main house
Workspace, lounge, meeting room and gallery
The main house uses its second and third floors. The workspace, lounge, meeting room and gallery are gathered on the third.
Because the old building's frame was kept, it has textures and shadows that new buildings lack.
The workspace in the main house
02 · Old residence
The private-office building
The old residence has private offices on its first and second floors. Members move across the site between the shared spaces of the main house and the closed rooms of the residence.
With two buildings, switching between focused time and time with others is as simple as walking from one to the other.
Moving between the two buildings
03 · Plans
Free desk, fixed desk and pop-in
A free desk is ¥42,350 a month and a fixed desk ¥60,500 a month, both with a ¥11,000 sign-up fee. Pop-in costs ¥3,300 a day, or ¥33,000 for an 11-day pack.
It is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, with a kitchen, lockers and free drinks.
A corner of the Nakameguro site

word.title: What is pop-in?
body: MIDORI.so's day-use option: ¥3,300 a day, or ¥33,000 for an 11-day pack.
It is a way to feel the place before signing a monthly contract. The 11-day pack also suits people who come only two or three days a week.

name: co-ba ebisu
card: A “liberated zone for work” across two floors and 1,573 m²
title: co-ba ebisu — a shared workplace across two floors and about 1,600 m² in Ebisu-nishi, built as a “liberated zone for work”
lead: co-ba ebisu is on the first and second floors of JP noie Ebisu-nishi, three minutes from Daikanyama Station and five from Ebisu Station. Opened in November 2019, it covers 1,573.42 m²: coworking on the first floor and private offices on the second. Its theme is “a liberated zone for work”, and its design theme is “WORK ASSEMBLE”. It is run by Ba & Co. Everything below is based on the official website.
hero_cap: PARK — an event space for up to 70 people
concept: A liberated zone for work, for adults with ambition

co-ba is “a shared workplace for every kind of challenge”: a network with directly run sites in Ebisu (Tokyo) and Kannai (Yokohama) and more than 18 partner sites from Iwate to Miyazaki. Ebisu is one of the directly run sites, presented as “a place where adults with ambition gather”.

The design theme, WORK ASSEMBLE, encourages people to assemble their own way of working and spending time. The first-floor coworking is open 24 hours, and the second floor has private offices on two-year fixed-term contracts.
steps: 01 · Park and café
PARK for 70, CAFE for 40
The first floor has two event spaces, PARK and CAFE. PARK holds up to 70 people and CAFE up to 40; members can rent them at half price.
Day to day they are shared spaces, booked out only for events — keeping work and connection on the same floor.
PARK — an event space for up to 70 people
CAFE — for smaller gatherings of up to 40
02 · 2F private offices
Rooms for 8 to 20 people
The second floor is for private offices. Single and twin rooms are about 31–34 m² for around 8 people; suites are about 48–72 m² for 10–20.
Contracts are two-year fixed terms, management fee included. Second-floor tenants can add first-floor coworking for ¥30,000 a month.
A second-floor private office (single room)
A second-floor private office (suite)

word.title: What does WORK ASSEMBLE mean?
body: co-ba ebisu's design theme. It means that people put together their own way of working and spending time.
Early mornings only, nights and weekends only, two days a month — a price list split by time of day turns this idea directly into contract options.

name: Business-Airport Aoyama
card: Two floors for free thinking, 3 minutes from Gaiemmae
title: Business-Airport Aoyama — a shared office opened by Tokyu Land in 2013, 3 minutes from Gaiemmae Station
lead: Business-Airport Aoyama is on the 4th and 6th floors of the Spline Aoyama Tokyu Building, a three-minute walk from Gaiemmae Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line. Business-Airport is Tokyu Land's brand of shared and rental offices, and Aoyama opened in March 2013. The official website calls it “a stylish workspace that sparks free thinking, in true Aoyama style”. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 5 rooms (A, B, A+B, C, D) + an online meeting room; event space for 60
hero_cap: Coworking seats with a view over Aoyama
concept: An “airport” where diverse people gather and take off

The name Business-Airport comes from international airports: a place where diverse people gather and depart. It expresses the hope that new businesses will take off from here and spread around the world. Run by Tokyu Land, the brand has 20 sites, including Marunouchi, Hibiya, Shinjuku, Shibuya, Yokohama and Osaka.

Staff are on site during reception hours and security is thorough. Community managers support members, and members of any site can use the coworking areas of every site. Aoyama aims to be “a stylish workspace that sparks free thinking, in true Aoyama style”.
steps: 01 · Coworking
Open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays
The coworking area is open 7:00–22:00 on weekdays and 10:00–18:00 on Sundays and holidays. Reception is staffed 9:00–18:00 on weekdays.
Window seats look out over Aoyama. Because it opens early, you can spend an hour here before heading to the office.
Coworking seats
02 · Meeting rooms
Five rooms, an online meeting room and an event space for 60
There are five meeting rooms — A, B, A+B, C and D — plus an online meeting room.
The event space holds up to 60 people, and there is a lounge and a break area.
Meeting room
03 · Private rooms
ROOM and BOOTH
Private spaces come in two types, ROOM and BOOTH, suited to using the site as a company base.
The brand-wide price list shows a serviced-office ROOM at ¥132,000 a month, a BOOTH at ¥110,000 and a DESK at ¥104,500.
A private workspace
04 · Location
3 minutes from exit 1a of Gaiemmae Station
It is on the 4th and 6th floors of the Spline Aoyama Tokyu Building, a three-minute walk from exit 1a of Gaiemmae Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line.
Opened in March 2013, it is one of the brand's earliest sites.
The route from Gaiemmae Station
Spline Aoyama Tokyu Building

word.title: What is a community manager?
body: A staff member who connects members with each other and with people outside, and who is the go-to person for events and questions. Business-Airport presents them as “partners who run alongside you”.
Their role differs from reception staff. Whether there is someone who manages seats or someone who introduces people changes how comfortable a shared office feels.

name: CIC Tokyo
card: Floors 15–16 of Toranomon Hills — about 6,000 m², one of the largest in Japan
title: CIC Tokyo — an innovation center of about 6,000 m² with more than 325 companies, on floors 15–16 of Toranomon Hills Business Tower
lead: CIC Tokyo is on the 15th and 16th floors of Toranomon Hills Business Tower, directly connected to Toranomon Hills Station on the Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line. It is the first Asian site of CIC, the innovation center founded in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in 1999. About 6,000 m² in total, it is home to more than 325 companies and individuals from Japan and abroad. Open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, it has 163 private offices, 100 coworking seats, meeting rooms and 24 phone booths. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 163 private offices (1–46 people) / 100 coworking seats / 24 phone booths
CIC Japan GK / CIC Toranomon GK (est. 2018)
hero_cap: Venture Café Tokyo — a café-like event space
concept: A launch base for innovation, built for entrepreneurs

CIC Tokyo calls itself “a launch base for innovation connected to the world”. It supports startups as they grow globally while building a dense community of innovators, investors and companies from around the world. Set in the heart of Toranomon, its roughly 6,000 m² make it one of the largest in Japan, according to the official website.

There are 163 private offices for 1–46 people, 100 coworking seats, meeting rooms and 24 phone booths. Meeting rooms, soundproof phone booths, kitchens, 24-hour building access, bilingual staff, a registrable business address, a wellness area and a game room are all included in the monthly fee. Members can also visit CIC sites around the world as guests at no extra cost.
steps: 01 · Venture Café and the 16F kitchen
A 300-person event space and two kitchens linked by a grand staircase
The community kitchen also works as part of an event space for up to 300 people. Every Thursday from 16:00, Venture Café Tokyo hosts its Thursday Gathering.
The 16th-floor kitchen is linked to the 15th-floor kitchen by a grand staircase. It is also used as part of the event space and, the website says, sparks new encounters between members.
Venture Café Tokyo — a café-like event space
The 16th-floor kitchen, linked to the 15th by a grand staircase
02 · Meeting rooms and living room
Meeting rooms each designed differently, and a living room of carefully chosen furniture
Meeting rooms seat 1 to 16 people, and each has its own design. They can be used without limit, and window-side rooms look out over Toranomon.
The living room is furnished with carefully selected pieces — for work, reading or lunch.
A meeting room — each has its own design
The living room — carefully chosen furniture for rest and work
03 · Wellness area and game room
From a nursing room and showers to table tennis
The wellness area has a nursing room, a massage room, a nap room and showers, meant to support members' wellbeing and fit around their lives.
The game room has video games, a table-tennis table and board games — a place to refresh, build teams and meet other members.
Wellness area — nursing room, massage room, nap room and showers
Game room — table tennis and board games
Toranomon Hills Business Tower from outside

word.title: What is Venture Café?
body: A sister organisation of CIC that runs events connecting entrepreneurs and supporters. At CIC Tokyo it hosts the Thursday Gathering every Thursday from 16:00.
A place to work and a weekly gathering on the same floor — that combination is why CIC is called a community rather than an office.

credits: CIC Tokyo (CIC Japan GK / CIC Toranomon GK)
CIC Japan official website: “CIC Tokyo”, “Office space”, “Coworking space”, “Events”, “About”

name: point 0 marunouchi
card: A green, experimental office run jointly by 19 major companies
title: point 0 marunouchi — a “future office” on the 4th floor of Marunouchi 2-chome Building, with interiors by Klein Dytham architecture
lead: A few minutes' walk from Tokyo Station, next to the Marunouchi Building, point 0 marunouchi is on the 4th floor of the Marunouchi 2-chome Building. Opened in July 2019, this members' coworking space is also a testbed for “the office of the future”. Companies such as Daikin, Okamura and Panasonic take part, and the interior was designed by Klein Dytham architecture. In January 2021 it became the first coworking office in Japan to earn WELL certification (WELL v2 pilot) at Gold level. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Klein Dytham architecture (planting by parkERs, branding by Insitu + artless)
hero_cap: A green workspace that seems to bring Marunouchi's trees indoors
concept: Towards the future of the office

point 0 is a place to keep asking what the office of the future should be. In an age when the lines between office and home, company and company, work and play are fading, it wants to redefine why people still gather in an office. Nineteen companies take part, including Daikin, Okamura, Panasonic, Lion, TOTO, Kajima and Mitsubishi Estate, collecting data on how people move and on the environment here to improve spaces and create new services.

The aim was “a green space that seems to bring Marunouchi's lush trees straight indoors”, with air, light, sound and scent that make the most of that greenery; uncompromising office furniture; elements of daily life such as showers and sleep; and food and drink that support good conversation. Interiors are by Klein Dytham architecture, planting by parkERs, and branding by Insitu and artless.
steps: 01 · Workspace and greenery
Seats surrounded by plants

Plants of many kinds are placed so people can relax as they work. There are 14 dedicated seats; free seating is available to monthly members or pay-as-you-go in 15-minute units. Both are open 24 hours, 365 days a year.

The official site lists a dedicated seat at ¥115,500 a month (12-month contract), a monthly free-seat membership at ¥82,500 a month (12-month contract), and drop-in use at ¥275 per 15 minutes (all including tax).
A workspace surrounded by plants
Seats facing the windows
02 · Café and community
Specialty coffee and an event space for 80
There is a café serving specialty coffee, and the website describes a rich community and events for shaping the future of work together.
The event space holds up to 80 people. There are various meeting rooms for different purposes: ¥3,300 an hour, or ¥6,600 an hour for the large room (including tax).
The café counter
An open area that also hosts events
03 · Rooms to focus and rest
Meditation room, focus booths, nap rooms and showers
The meditation room is for meditation, yoga, or thinking in a different setting. There are also private focus booths that block sound and sightlines.
Nap booths for better productivity, free showers open 24 hours and a free low-oxygen room complete the floor. Work and rest happen side by side.
A room for focus
A room for rest
04 · IoT and experiments
Experience the future office

IoT devices are installed throughout, so you can experience the office of the future. Partner companies bring their latest technology, data and know-how to the open space, meeting rooms and nap booths.
Data on movement, vital signs and equipment operation is collected and analysed to improve the space and create new services. Simply by sitting here, you take part in the experiment.
The shared space

word.title: What is WELL Certification?
body: A rating system for buildings that adds human health to the design, construction and operation of a space. Started by the US-based IWBI in 2014, it assesses ten concepts: air, water, nourishment, light, movement, thermal comfort, sound, materials, mind and community.

point 0 marunouchi earned WELL v2 pilot Gold in January 2021 — a first for a coworking office in Japan — achieved, the website says, with technology from Daikin (air and space), Okamura (furniture) and Panasonic (lighting).

credits: point 0 official website (point0.work): “our drive”, “space”, “price”, “company”; point 0 corporate site: “point 0 marunouchi”

name: MIDORI.so NAGATACHO
card: A whole building from B1 to 6F — MIDORI.so's flagship
title: MIDORI.so NAGATACHO — MIDORI.so's seven-floor flagship in Nagatacho, for teams of 1 to 150
lead: MIDORI.so NAGATACHO is at Hirakawacho 2-5-3, a two-minute walk from Nagatacho Station. MIDORI.so's flagship uses an entire building — seven floors from B1 to 6F, about 23,000 sq ft — and can host teams from 1 to 150 people. The second floor has a 212 m² engagement space for team meetings, meetups, pop-up offsite offices and mixers. Its operator, MIRAI INSTITUTE, runs eight sites in Tokyo. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Seven floors from B1 to 6F, about 23,000 sq ft (per the official site)
hero_cap: MIDORI.so's flagship, occupying a whole building in Hirakawacho
concept: FUTURE DIVERSITY

MIDORI.so is a coworking community exploring “the future of work in a society that values the individual”. Beyond freelancers and startups, it is for people who try to stay independent inside large organisations and people who want to create new value, the website says.

The building was originally run as Nagatacho GRiD. MIRAI INSTITUTE took over the whole building in May 2023 and reopened it, expanded, as MIDORI.so NAGATACHO on 1 November 2023 under the concept “FUTURE DIVERSITY”. It is the flagship alongside the Nakameguro, Bakuro-yokoyama, Shibuya, Aoyama, Ikejiri, Kichijoji and Nihonbashi sites.
steps: 01 · 5F workspace
A shared floor with a kitchen, lounge, beds and a library

The fifth floor is shared. Along with the workspace, meeting rooms, kitchen and lounge, there are beds and a library. Window seats, sofas and bookshelves let you change how you work on a single floor.

A free desk is ¥42,350 a month and a fixed desk ¥60,500 a month (both with an ¥11,000 sign-up fee, including tax), available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. Ten hours of meeting rooms a month are included, and you can register your company here.
The 5th-floor lounge
02 · 5F library
Working surrounded by books
The fifth-floor library is surrounded by bookshelves — a place to read and to work.
Pop-in costs ¥3,300 a day or ¥33,000 for an 11-day pack, using any free seat on weekdays from 10:00 to 18:00. It is a way to try the floor before becoming a member.
The 5th-floor library
The 5th-floor workspace
03 · 2F engagement space
212 m², 80 seated or 100 standing
The second-floor engagement space is for deepening ties with the community: team meetings, meetups, offsite offices for a few days, mixers and programmes that raise engagement in organisations.

It is 212.0 m² and holds up to 80 seated or 100 standing. With a bar counter, fridge, projector, screen, sound system and Wi-Fi, it can be rented 9:00–22:00 for ¥385,000 a day or ¥55,000 an hour (¥38,500 an hour for 6 hours or more, all including tax).
The 2nd-floor engagement space
The engagement space with its bar counter

word.title: What is the engagement space?
body: A bookable room on the second floor of MIDORI.so NAGATACHO, made for deepening ties with the community. It is used for team meetings, meetups and offsite offices for a limited number of days.
Placing a room for outside teams inside the members' workplace increases how often members and outsiders meet in the same building.

credits: MIDORI.so official website: “Nagatacho”, “About”; MIRAI INSTITUTE press release (14 September 2023)

name: SHARE M-10
card: Designed by Kengo Kuma — a forest-like room ringed by stacked timber planters
title: SHARE M-10 — a forest-like coworking space by Kengo Kuma, one minute from Azabu-Juban Station
lead: SHARE M-10 is on the 2nd and 3rd floors of MAXPLAN AZABU10, which stands at the Ichinohashi intersection a one-minute walk from Azabu-Juban Station. Both the building and the interior were designed by architect Kengo Kuma. The second floor is a 16-seat coworking space and the third a meeting room for up to 10 people. Billed as “a place for coexistence and creation”, it lets you work in a café-like atmosphere. Everything below is based on the official website and the architect's project page.
hero_cap: A workspace ringed by planters made of stacked timber rings
concept: A free, soft space — the opposite of a closed office

According to the architect's project page, SHARE M-10 is a shared office inside MAXPLAN AZABU10 (2020), a building by the same firm. The Ichinohashi intersection in Azabu-Juban is where working, living and shopping meet; there, the firm created a free, soft space that is the opposite of a closed office.

The room is surrounded by planters made of stacked timber rings, which make the shared office feel like a forest. The official site describes it as “a place for coexistence and creation” and “coworking and meeting rooms that feel like a café”.
steps: 01 · 2F coworking
16 seats surrounded by timber-ring planters
The second floor is a 16-seat coworking space. Planters of stacked timber rings surround the seats, so you work among the greenery.
Carefully chosen coffee and other drinks are provided, and entry is linked to the Akerun smart lock.
Seats surrounded by timber-ring planters and plants
The 2nd-floor workspace
02 · Air and windows
HEPA-filtered ventilation and Low-E double glazing
The official website says the space has a 24-hour ventilation system with HEPA filters.
The windows use Low-E double glazing to reduce energy use. In a room full of plants, the quality of the air is also looked after.
Window seats
A workspace filled with soft light
03 · 3F meeting room
A meeting room for 10, and whole-floor hire
The third floor is a meeting room for up to 10 people.
The floor can also be hired exclusively, for 30 people with 21 seats (up to 25). Exclusive bookings are accepted up to one week in advance.
An interior wrapped in wood

word.title: What is Low-E double glazing?
body: Window glass made of two panes with a layer of air between them and a special metal coating on the surface. It keeps out the heat of summer sun and keeps indoor warmth from escaping in winter.
The bigger the windows, the more the glass decides how comfortable a room feels. SHARE M-10 pairs its green interior with good windows and ventilation.
